status: FROZEN before any job of this experiment runs. It is the one methodological refinement of Gate X: delivery plus one captured check, measured directly in both treatments. bench/total_run.py prints this file's sha256 in every job and bench/total_analyze.py refuses any other. Changing it after a job ran starts a new experiment, and none is planned: a FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE or INCOMPLETE result stands.
question: Does a job that receives the packaged Rust candidate and checks the typical capture with it reach the end of that check sooner than the same job receiving the frozen Python package and checking the same capture with it?
scope: Runner delivery of one first-party snapshot plus one captured hidden-Unicode check of the typical 889-line capture, with the setup both treatments share. Not Git acquisition, event parsing, identity or attribution checks, not the complete action, not a job or billing forecast.
label: native-total-cost

candidate.work: bash --noprofile --norc -- <delivered>/experiments/native-distribution/launch.sh, the composite step's own command, with AGX_CAPTURE, RUNNER_OS=Linux, GITHUB_ACTION_PATH=<delivered>/experiments/native-distribution and a RUNNER_TEMP the worker owns: platform selection, private extraction of the delivered gzip asset, the native drive, removal of its directory.

control.work: <python 3.14> -I -B bench/py_driver.py <delivered> faithful drive <capture>: the captured-driver adapter of the accepted measurement, bound to its bytes at the candidate snapshot, driving the delivered agent_guardrails package (also checked by tools/baseline.py). The root action's full Git check is not run: its event contract and work differ from a capture-only check.

expected.source: Every python-faithful and rust-packaged trial of pr-typical in the accepted run 36487178769, both architectures.

python.use: actions/setup-python 3.14 in every job of both treatments. It runs the worker in both and the control's check; it is shared setup, not a requirement of the candidate.

order: bench/total_plan.first_order(seed, pairs), recorded in first below before any job ran: one architecture has candidate first in four pairs, the other in three. Per architecture one chain of 14 jobs, pair 1's first treatment, then its second, then pair 2, each needing the previous job, so the two jobs of a pair run close together. They are fresh hosted VMs, not one machine. The two chains may run at the same time.

search.root: The common ancestor of RUNNER_TEMP and GITHUB_WORKSPACE after resolving both, refused when it is / or contains HOME.
search.rule: Directories only, symlinks never followed, GITHUB_WORKSPACE (this checkout, which holds a copy of the candidate) and RUNNER_TEMP never entered. Exactly one directory named by the treatment's full SHA, directly under <delivered_as>, and none named by the other treatment's SHA or a symlink named by either. Every regular file below it must equal the manifest, path for path and byte for byte, and nothing else may be there. No fallback: anything else leaves that job, and so its pair, incomplete.

fresh_delivery: Every job is a fresh hosted VM that downloads its one snapshot during Set up job; nothing prewarms it. The worker records the runner's .completed watermark beside the delivered directory and refuses a delivery the runner's action archive cache (ACTIONS_RUNNER_ACTION_ARCHIVE_CACHE) could have served.

boundaries.start: The runner's own 'Getting action download info' line in Set up job, before any action and so before the first-party snapshot is downloaded.
boundaries.end: The worker's end marker line, which it prints only after the check exited, its status and output were captured and compared, and its owned directory was removed.
boundaries.total: end minus start in the runner's log timestamps (100 ns resolution, kept as exact integers). Everything between is included: every action download, checkout, Python setup, capture generation, worker start, discovery, manifest check, the check itself and cleanup.
boundaries.markers: agx-total begin/end lines with one JSON object each: a fresh nonce, run, attempt, job, arch, pair, position, treatment, snapshot, source commit, workflow ref, case, contract sha256, and the worker's wall clock (time.time_ns) and monotonic durations (perf_counter_ns).

known_asymmetries: The manifest check hashes the whole delivered tree, 76 files for the candidate against 38 for the control, so it costs the candidate a few milliseconds more. It stays inside the total: it is how the job proves which bytes ran.
The control's check starts the same interpreter the worker is running, with its standard library already in the page cache; that favours the control.
Both treatments run the worker, the adapter check and the capture generation, so neither is charged for them alone.

clock.rule: Within a job every log timestamp is nondecreasing in log order; each marker's log timestamp trails the wall clock the worker printed in it by 0 to max_marker_lag_ms; the log interval between the two markers agrees with the worker's monotonic interval within max_worker_log_disagreement_ms. The retained transfer run's 112 printed marks trailed their log stamps by 0.154 to 2.637 ms. A violation is a clock anomaly: that result is INCONCLUSIVE, never a measurement.

decision.difference: Per architecture and pair: total(candidate) minus total(control) of that pair's two jobs.
decision.timestamp_uncertainty: The end marker's log stamp trails the worker's own end by its observed lag. A pair's difference is therefore known to lie within [difference - lag(candidate end) - 4 resolution, difference + lag(control end) + 4 resolution]: two stamps per total, two totals.
decision.architecture_verdict: PASS when the median of the seven differences is below zero and the largest difference is below zero, also at the upper end of its timestamp uncertainty. FAIL when the smallest difference is zero or more, also at the lower end of its uncertainty: no pair shows a benefit. INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
decision.outcome: INCOMPLETE when any declared job is missing, not successful, cancelled, timed out, attempted more than once, or fails any identity, delivery, output or cleanup check; no job or pair is replaced or rerun. Otherwise INCONCLUSIVE on any clock anomaly. Otherwise PASS when both architectures PASS, FAIL when both FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE otherwise, including disagreement.
decision.boundary: Zero is the no-erasure boundary: the captured-check gain is not established if delivery and the matched surrounding work consume it. No percentage allowance of a long shared setup step.
decision.sign_test: If the seven differences were independent draws from one continuous distribution, [min, max] would cover their median with probability 1 - 2 * 0.5^7 = 98.4375%. Hosted VMs, scheduling and a shared service do not establish independence or stationarity, so this is an operational decision rule, not a confidence guarantee.
decision.stop: Seven pairs per architecture, once. No eighth pair, no outlier removal, no pooling with the transfer experiment, the captured-driver rounds or any later CI run. FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE or INCOMPLETE ends the Rust full-port recommendation under the current plan.

diagnostics: preparation: 'Getting action download info' to 'Complete job name', and the first-party download line to the line after it
the worker's discovery, manifest check, check process (spawn to reap), cleanup and its whole run, from its monotonic clock
the whole non-queue job, first to last log line, and the Jobs API queue time in whole seconds
runner name, id and labels, the .completed watermark, the archive cache state
Diagnostics are reported beside the total, never subtracted from it or added to other experiments' medians.
captured_driver_result: The accepted captured-driver PASS (contract.json, sha256 05cbf35c40bffe66ee86eacfe55b9f364c75b210e43ca8210dbf7b0a20ab5dbc, run 36487178769) stays a separate result with its own criteria. This experiment neither repeats nor replaces it.
remaining_gap: The deployed action runs python3 -I run.py from the runner's own Python and fetches and checks Git data, the event and attribution; the control here runs CPython 3.14 on a capture. Neither treatment measures that work, so a PASS here is no full-action or job no-regression result.
not_measured: Git acquisition, event parsing, identity and attribution checks
the complete action or job, or billing
queue and runner allocation time, which is recorded only
